content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target).**

Garman owns all IP in the Work — including the Improvements and the Schedule "D" Modifications we fund (§13) — while our only right is a non-transferable, non-exclusive licence tied to AS400s at Authorized Locations (§2), expressly non-sublicensable (§3(c)), lasting only while fees are paid and the Agreement is not terminated (§17(a)). Vendor ownership of its own platform is acceptable, but the licence back fails the fallback on four material terms (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free) and omits modification and sublicensing rights. Nothing in the document limits Garman's use of our converted data (§4(b)).

Redline (validated, ok:true), three surgical operations:
1. §2 grant reworked to a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence to use, modify and sublicense for our business — with the location limit and extra-fee sentence removed as contradictory to "worldwide"/"royalty-free".
2. §3(c) sublicence prohibition deleted (retaining the assignment, lease and export restrictions verbatim) so the new grant is not self-defeating.
3. New §4(c) limiting any licence to Garman in our data to processing solely to provide the services.

Garman's retained ownership of the Work satisfied the first fallback element already, so no ownership language was added.
